title: First New Orleans job at the Pelican with Pop Silverstein
summary: First job in New Orleans was at the Pelican with Papa Celestin, via her husband the drummer.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: They may be doing it now, but they didn't. They sound like he was on the new, were you saying that? Yeah. Well anyway, that's enough of that old music stuff, until we get between the reels. Then we'll play a little four handed. Can you play bass while I play treble? Mm-hmm. Okay. Play bass while you play treble. Yeah. Go ahead, Joel. All right. Now you came here, you said in 1920. Uh-huh. What was the first place you played when you came to New Orleans? When I first came to New Orleans, I played at the Pelican. That was my first job I played. Who were you with? Pop Silverstein.

That's the first job? Did you know him from Pensacola? No, I met him through in Chinese, because Chinese played drums with him. And Chinese was my husband at that time. So he had sent for Jeanette the cup. So I was on the boat playing then. Already when you first got here you were?
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. And he used to play that number by my Joelis Feeze. And then when he sent for Janet, Janet came. And then I played with pops up there. We always were friends, you know. Come down to the Chinese house, his mother, and she cooked and all that. And then the next thing I was playing, I was playing from one band to another. And the nights when I wasn't on the boat playing, I would maybe play some bill guard and somebody else would get me to play piano.
